text: Flying discs are a type of magical device used for personal transportation, most commonly utilized by mages or other spellcasters. Some enemies who utilize flying discs will leave their disc behind when slain, allowing enterprising adventurers to temporarily ride them.

The Forbidden Reach is an island located off the coast of the Dragon Isles. It was fashioned by Neltharion the Earth-Warder to serve as a training ground for his ultimate soldiers, the dracthyr. But in the aftermath of a terrible battle, the island has lain dormant and abandoned for ages until the return of an ancient enemy causes the dracthyr to stir. The zone is the starting zone of the new playable race-hero class combo dracthyr evoker starting at level 58. Until patch 10.0.7 when the zone was re-opened, when a player visited the Forbidden Reach outside of the evoker starting experience by flying from the mainland Dragon Isles, they were struck by lightning until they died.

The Forlorn Rowe is located in northwestern Duskwood, on the northern edge of Raven Hill Cemetery. It is a hill cloaked in an ominous darkness, upon which the home of Morbent Fel rests, the powerful necromancer who rules the forest's undead creatures through evil arcane magic. Alliance-aligned adventurers will need to do a lot of running and fighting in order to obtain the only special weapon that could stop him. Following Morbent Fel's defeat against the Adventurers, Commander Ladimore placed the :Torch of Holy Flame right in front of the necromancer's home to dispelling dark enchantments and keeping the undead docile in Duskwood. The Forge of the Guardian is the artifact forge for mages of the Tirisgarde. An artifact of incredible power, it was used for centuries by the Council of Tirisfal to transfer the arcane power of many mages into the body of one, thus creating a Guardian of Tirisfal. It was first devised by Alodi, the first Guardian, whose spirit is forever bound to the forge, allowing him to interact with the people of the present centuries after his death. The Forge of the Guardian also serves as a font of arcane energy which can be used to manipulate and empower the artifacts of the world. Forsaken Bats serve as the Undercity's equivalent of an air force, patrolling the city from the higher levels to dispose of enemy intruders. It will dismount such enemies with a sonic blast. When the Forsaken retook the Ruins of Lordaeron, the bats began patrolling the city's skies. Some of them are wounded and tended to by Michael Garrett.

The fortress was also home to a mystic sanctum where a dark order of death knights dwelt. Its towering spires reached upwards as obsidian blades to cleave the hostile amber skies above.

Fortitude of the Bear is a Tenacity hunter pet ability that temporarily increases the maximum health of the hunter and their pet. It is available to all hunter specs as long as their current pet is a Tenacity pet. It's also available to Marksmanship hunters talented into Lone Wolf who do not have a pet by their side via Command Pet.

Fray Island is a small arid island located off the eastern shore of the Northern Barrens. A small sewer stretches the length of the island and players diving into it will be able to find several fish.

Frostfire refers to a type of magic wielded by mages. It is a multi-school, combining the Fire and Frost schools, even though these are often the opposite of each other. Multi-school abilities benefit from bonuses that affect any of their schools, use the lowest resistance value among their schools, ignore absorption and immunity effects that apply to only some of their schools, and can be used even when one or more of their schools have been locked with an interrupt effect. For example, Frostfire spells have the ability to apply both DoT's used by fire spells, and chills used by frost spells.

According to Muradin Bronzebeard, it's a place to see icebergs from the size of houses to the size of islands floating along, and the strong, biting winds make for choppy waters at the best of times. As Freya sculpted the Emerald Dream to act as a guide for Azeroth's natural life, she crafted and planted one tree near the powerful energy of the Vale of Eternal Blossoms in Pandaria. It grew strong and tall, drinking deeply from the vale's resonant power. More trees rose around it, and lush forests, both in the Emerald Dream and the waking world, sprang to life across the region. Funny Bunny is a bunny of Bunny Island. He is known as the "Easter Bunny" and gives easter eggs to those who catch him. He is at odds with the "evil bunnies" of Bunny Island. He may also be the one that leaves easter eggs all over Azeroth. Funny Bunny is capable of turning visitors, often children, into bunnies in order to help them better collect the eggs he has scattered around the island.

After being held for a short time, this item will attract a Bitestone Fishbrul which, when killed, will drop a Salmon Lure. The lure can then be used as bait to catch Ancient Highmountain Salmon. If one already has the Underlight Angler, they will instead catch Ancient Highmountain Salmon.

Fyldan is a night elf cooking vendor located in the Craftsmen's Terrace in the night elf city of Darnassus. During the Burning of Teldrassil, he was caught in the chaos and could be saved. As of Dragonflight, he can be seen floating around as a wisp in the city of Bel'Amath, Amirdrassil. It is unknown what has happened to him.

Gaeval Thunderblast is a gnome ace in service of the Alliance. Swooping along in his flying machine, preying on bandits and other evildoers, Gaeval is a gnome of unparalleled skill in the air; he has only lost once or twice in his long life. Part of an elite group of aces known as the Thundering Rockets, Gaeval claims he has more stories under his belt than half the dwarves who fought during the Third War. While he could not fight in the Third War due to difficulties in his homeland, he regrets both the loss of his city to the troggs and his inability to do anything for the Alliance in its greatest time of need. An Old God once landed on the planet, its impact destroying an entire kingdom and disrupting the balance of nature. The area around it became a wasteland from which none returned. Though Fyzandi's druids kept watch from the border, the Old God soon spawned an army of horrific monsters: creatures with too many limbs, hungering mouths, and too many eyes. Garhan Stornhorn was a legendary Highmountain tauren leatherworker in Highmountain. He made first true leather armor of the Highmountain tribes.

The genesaur are a race of colossal and immensely powerful plant-like demigods native to Draenor. They are the dominant race of the collective of plant creatures known as the Primals, and are worshipped as deities by their lesser relatives. While not the most powerful genesaur encountered, Iyu is the most directly antagonistic and the one who most directly commands the botani. The genesaur were hunted to extinction by the Old Horde in the main universe, but they are still present in the Draenor of an alternate timeline.

Ghostly Citizens are human ghosts located in Stratholme. They perished when the city was devastated by Arthas Menethil, but don't even seem to realize they are dead. They were active even during the Burning Legion's third invasion and when the Silver Hand attacked the city.
The Giant Moonwillow Cone is found at northwest of the great tree on Moonwillow Peak in west-central . It contains the Moonwillow Wand and 10-20x Garrison Resources.

Gilnean Envoys were Forsaken Battle for Gilneas recruiters located at various spots throughout the largest Horde cities - Orgrimmar, Silvermoon City, Thunder Bluff, and Undercity. They only appeared during the monthly Call to Arms: Battle for Gilneas.

Gimp is a slang term, adapted for use in game terms from the slang word gimp, meaning to walk with a limp or be a person with limited use of their leg/legs. This term should probably be considered rude and inappropriate. *In the game, the term "gimp" would refer to: **a player who is wearing gear is far below their level, or whose gear is useless to them. **the action of severely diminishing a value or set of abilities, perhaps for the purpose of strengthening another value or ability.
The Girdle of Beastial Fury is a leather belt which boosts strength, stamina, and attack power. The bonus to attack power make this item a favorite of rogues.

Gino is a goblin quest giver located in Storm Peaks. He is on top of the mountain near the teleporter. He can be seen after completing quests with Tore Rumblewrench, after which, the teleporter in K3 takes the player to him. He was criticized by the Inventor's League for all of his inventions blowing up, though he himself took pride in it.

Gladiator: Dragonflight Season 1 is a feat of strength achievement earned by winning 50 3v3 games while at Elite rank during Dragonflight Season 1.

__NOTOC__ Glomp is a ogre located on Fray Island in the Northern Barrens. He is the Treasurer of the Southsea Freebooters. After the Theramore's Fall, Jaina Proudmoore traveled to Fray Island, from where she wanted to launch her assault on Orgrimmar. To avoid being distracted, she killed all the pirates of the island, including Glomp.

Gnarlgar was a treant who dwelled in Talador around 2,000 years before the opening of the Dark Portal. It was one of Talador's most powerful primals, and it commanded immense power over nature magic as well as the Spirit of Life that flowed through the wilds. Seeing the Apexis arakkoa as a threat to the wilds, Gnarlgar united the primals, oversaw the creation of the new Sporemound Taala and created the Gnarled to wage war upon the Apexis, but its efforts ultimately failed thanks to the joint efforts of the Anhari and Skalaxi arakkoa orders.
Gnomeregan Gnuggets were sold by Rona Greenteeth on Darkmoon Island during the Darkmoon Faire for .

The Gnomes of Khaz Modan have long offset their lack of physical strength with ingenuity and daring. As members of the Alliance, they have continued to display their talents by inventing and piloting the unbelievable Flying Machine. Although having no armaments, these awkward contraptions can be used to survey vast areas of terrain, and detecting the otherwise hidden movements of underwater units (as all flying units can), making them invaluable for discovering the movements of the Horde.

__NOTOC__ Gol Inath is a hollow tree located at the center of the Crimson Forest in southwestern Drustvar. It is the staging ground where the witches build their construct army, leeching their powers from the ancient magic of the Drust. The entrance to Thros, the Blighted Lands is found inside the tree. The ancient Drust worshiped it. It is here where Gorak Tul is summoned by the Heartsbane Coven. It may be connected to the same location as The Rupture in Waycrest Manor as it uses the exact same architecture. Later, it is in control of some "Briarbane" Drust under the command of Gorak Zhar, protecting the Flame of Oblivion, which contains a portion of Gorak Tul's power.

Goldwing is an eagle and is one of many animals featured in the Darkmoon Faire zoo on Darkmoon Island.
Goliath Offline is a dungeon & raid achievement earned by activating and destroying all three Shattered Devastators and then kill Oryphrion on Mythic Difficulty.

Golden Path is a conduit for paladins. It drops from Hylbrande in Tazavesh, the Veiled Market, Lady Inerva Darkvein in Castle Nathria, and Skolex in the Sepulcher of the First Ones. An ilvl 145 version is also rewarded from Strengthen the Bond, A Journey Made Together, Strengthening the Bond (Night Fae), and Strengthening the Bond (Venthyr).
Goods from Silvermoon City is part of the Blood Elf only quest chain that introduces players to using the flight paths.

Goria ("Throne of the King" in the ogre language) was the ancient capital of the ogres and the Gorian Empire up until around 400 years before the opening of the Dark Portal. Nestled near several hills, the city had thousands of inhabitants and an ocean port. It was built on former Apexis arakkoa territory, and later the draenei would build Shattrath City in the same location.

The Great Bear Spirit is a spirit bear found in Moonglade, due west along the mountains from Nighthaven. Said to be as old as the world, this noble being served as a mentor for young druids, teaching them their first true understanding of the bear. With its wisdom and blessings, they could learn to become druids of the Claw. In the Emerald Nightmare raid, the Great Bear Spirit is found dead in the Nightmare version of Moonglade.

Delegations from Silvermoon and the Undercity reside within, including paladin and priest trainers, as well as the trainer for archaeology.

Growless Cave is a cave in the Alterac Mountains that is home to mountain yeti. Occasionally Skhowl can be found just outside the entrance. Inside the cave used to be the Flame of Uzel, a ceremonial pyre created by a human named Helcular, it was to be used in his ritual to become a lich. The powerful yeti Frostmaw used approach the cave if meat is burned upon the Flame of Uzel. However, the flame has since been removed.

The Hangar can be found on the eastern side of the Isle of Conquest, situated on a bluff high above the Workshop. The Hangar's capture flag is near the north end of the bluff, closer to the Horde Keep. To gain access to the gunships, the controlling faction one of the two teleporters on the perimeter of the hangar itself, or the teleporter near the capture flag. Immunity is an avoidance mechanic available to both players and NPCs. It can be triggered by both items and spells, and it is also sometimes native. When immune to a spell or ability, a player will not be affected by neither its damage nor any secondary effect triggered by it. Temporary immunity also clears out all debuffs of the affected schools. Abilities such as Divine Shield and Ice Block grant temporary total immunity in nearly all cases, and purges them of most debuffs including snares, roots and stuns, although exceptionally potent abilities such as Mass Dispel can still remove the effect. They eventually defeated the Burning Legion.

Karsius the Ancient Watcher is a ghostly draenei who has been tasked with watching over the spirit of Teron Gorefiend. Gorefiend, in the guise of an Ancient Shadowmoon Spirit, convinces players to obtain his powerful regalia — his cloak, his armor, and his truncheon. The Keggary is a section on the upper floor of the Horde-faction city of Shrine of Two Moons in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. It contains many kegs of brew, as well as shelves of books and scrolls. It connects to the Imperial Mercantile to the north and a balcony of Hall of the Crescent Moon to the southwest, which contains an inn. A stairway leads down to Summer's Rest inn.

The Isle of Kezan (pronounced "KEH-zawn") located in the South Seas is the tropical homeland of the goblins. Their capital of Undermine is located beneath the island, deep in the bowels of Mount Kajaro. Thanks to Kezan's prominence as a mercantile hub, it's been divided into dozens of districts by the trade princes, who view every inch of land as an opportunity waiting to be converted into gold and silver. Kezan's tropical palms are bisected with miles of roadway, and even the beaches are beginning to be paved over by goblin ambitions. Kerri Hicks is a human quest giver found on Darkmoon Island. She now dual-wields two Darkmoon Hammers.

Kerxan is an ancient and powerful world that was conquered by the Burning Legion. The planet was home to a race of giants, four of which—Bahmethra, Hrestimorak, Salaranga, and Nilganihmaht—seized power through cunning and treachery and enacted a brutal thousand-year reign. They murdered countless rivals, weakening their own forces in the process. When the Legion arrived, the armies of Kerxan were too depleted to defy them, and even the four giants fell to the demons. After their deaths, the souls of the four were condemned to the Maw for their crimes. During the Legion's third invasion of Azeroth, Overseer Ingra used the :Scepter of Kerxan to summon Legion forces to Suramar.

Kola Watermane is a Highmountain tauren innkeeper and member of the Rivermane tribe found at Riverbend in Highmountain. She remains there even after most of the village is destroyed.

Kota Peak is an inhospitable mountain southwest of Kota Basecamp in western Kun-Lai Summit, just east of the Serpent's Spine. To the north via the Shado-Li Basin is Winter's Blossom, while Firebough Nook is to the south via the Yaungol Advance. The mountain is inhabited by mountain goats and yetis, which normally keep out of the way of grummles collecting Kafa'kota berries for the Keenbean Kafa Co. However, Cousin Gootfur came up with the hare-brained idea of feeding the goats berries in a lazy attempt to use the goats' digestive processes to gather seeds. Now the goats are Kafa-crazed, as are the yetis that traditionally eat the goats...

Lake Ere'Noru is located in southeastern Terokkar Forest, below the large mountain valley that houses Skettis. It is only available to those who have flight. She submerged herself in the temple's pool, and then went outside, returning soon after, and reporting that everything was on fire and that the roads into the city were blocked by the fire. Lasan Skyhorn (pronounced "LUH-sawn") is the chieftain of the Skyhorn tribe, one of the four tribes of the Highmountain tauren. He is almost always accompanied by his giant eagle mount, Aviash. Unlike his fellow chieftains, Lasan is a boisterous and jolly individual. He enjoys flying as much as a good fight. Lasan and his tribe regularly clash with the harpies of Highmountain.

A level cap is the maximum level a player character can reach in-game. With the release of Dragonflight, this is level 70. The level cap is changed with the release of each expansion. The level cap represents the ultimate goal and culmination of the leveling process, with max-level characters having gained access to all class abilities and talents, and being able to access end-game content and equip the most powerful gear. By providing an equal limit for the progression of all characters, the level cap allows for competitive and balanced gameplay in both PvE and PvP. Lev'al Rock Isle is a small island in the fatigue zone off the southern coast of the Azure Span. Its rocky landscape is littered with dead plantlife, piles of bones, and viscera. Crabs populate the island, wearing dragon skulls and vertebrae on their backs. The largest crab, Crustosteo, lurks within a cave; the smaller ones form the illusion of skeletal serpents by marching in single-file lines. Small fires dot Lev'al Rock Isle, burning at tree stumps and scraggy bushes. These fires were likely started by the Kindlets and Magma Slugs found in tiny caves across the island.

Liches are powerful undead beings. On Azeroth, they are usually bound to the iron will of the Lich King, they mainly wield frost magic and necromantic spells. Typically appearing as large, floating, skeletal figures wrapped in long robes, they are often found in high-ranking positions within the Scourge. Lieutenant Aden is a human quest giver located on Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh. He always volunteered for gate duty. Some time before the Shattering, a flood occurred in Theramore and Lady Jaina ordered Aden to open the door of Theramore's citadel for anyone who needed refuge. He was killed during the Attack on Theramore Isle, when the Horde destroyed the city with a mana bomb. His corpse was found on top of a roof and his armor turned purple-black from the blast.

A variety of lions known as mountain lions usually roam the warm mountain regions and plains of high terrain. As predators, lions tend to be and will attack players who approach them. They are the fiercest of predators in the Barrens. The lions that stalk amongst the tall grass do so with cunning, stealth, and power. The Longclaw tribe is a tribe of furbolgs inhabiting Longclaw Island at the westernmost point of the Azure Span. They came to the island, seeking shelter from the elemental corruption of the mainland. Tullek the tuskarr has taught members of the tribe how to fish. The Lothalor Woodlands is in the southwest corner of the Dragonblight just west of Indu'le Village. The land has been destroyed by the arcane energies pouring out, for this reason the ancients there have grown insane. The cause is the blue dragonflight, who, led by Lieutenant Ta'zinni, resides there, empowering a ley-line focus.

Lost Peak is the gigantic volcano at the center of the Lost Isles. The main path into the volcanic mountain lies on the western side of the main island, though there is also a tunnel entrance from Oomlot Village which cannot be accessed directly by the players. It has a massive caldera in which there is another smaller one. The fire turtle Volcanoth lived in its lair inside of the volcano. The goblins that got stranded on the Lost Isles built a mine on its northern foothills. After Volcanoth's death, Lost Peak erupted destroying much of the Lost Isles.
